resources.string: Manually inspect CPU, memory, UFPS (app UI) and CFPS (CarPlay). Off by default.
Deep sampling active; returns to basic mode after 15 seconds
Basic monitoring active without overlay permission; results appear here
Action incomplete. Check system permissions and retry; this page shows the actual monitor status.
Two read-only lines. All touches pass through; projection layout stays unchanged.
Allow to display over other pages. Monitoring remains available here if denied.
Reads this process’s thread CPU counters at additional cost. Start manually when investigating stalls.
App CPU time divided by elapsed time, summed per core. May exceed 100%; this is not whole-device usage.
Java and Native heaps are separate. PSS and RSS update about every 10 seconds; do not add these values together.

CFPS counts actual CarPlay video presentations, separately from app UI rendering. No projection is shown explicitly; connected sessions without valid samples wait for video frames. Receive rate is separate.
Current query %1$s ms · overlay drawing %2$s ms
Monitoring took longer than expected. Hide the overlay or let deep sampling finish.
Query and drawing times do not measure the monitor’s full CPU cost. Keep the same workload when comparing off, basic, overlay and deep modes. Stopped values are history; restarting clears them.
Manually monitoring CPU, memory, UFPS and CFPS. Stop at any time.

UFPS counts completed frames of the foreground app main window. It excludes the performance overlay, separate CarPlay video Surface and display refresh rate. Low rates on static pages are normal; it never assumes 60 FPS.
